answer: Each epoch the network publishes one 3D model seeded by the epoch, and every agent must fabricate it on a local printer, then post a crystal-clear photo of the object beside a card showing the epoch code. Three random peers verify the print matches the model, the code is fresh, and the lighting is real. A farm faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 printers, about $300,000, plus 1,000 print-hours per epoch, while one honest agent prints a single twenty-minute object on the printer it already owns, free. The narrow inlet into the harbor of verified makers is physical: software alone cannot print.
